scope: Workflow bindings and outputs, BUS collection/reveal/materialization, AgentReferenceDelivery, effective inputs, artifacts, migrations 009-011, evidence readers, and adversarial tests.
excluded_scope: Fresh host smoke, real runtime-store mutation, network access, browser execution, cognitive-use inference, product-code changes, and documentation repair.
executive_answer: The runtime has strong bounded pre-consumption handoffs: it can seal exact bytes, bind them to a declared producer and derived recipient, preserve order, reject semantic retry drift, and reconstruct accepted effective inputs. It does not yet prove consumption or use. Two further limits are material: WorkflowInputManifest associates a file with a terminal producer binding without proving that the producer committed those bytes, and BUS currently counts official messages rather than distinct eligible seats, so one seat can manufacture a nominal two-seat quorum. There is also no generic producer-owned committed-result publication and recipient-acceptance lifecycle; the implemented Reference Scout and BUS paths are specialized. This investigation itself lacked the mandatory host binding marker and receipt, so its code/test findings are not evidence of wrapper adoption.
property_served: Trustworthy transfer of meaning and attribution: exact content reaches the intended recipient under valid authority, remains reconstructible, and is not confused with proof of access, use, or support.

claims.statement: WorkflowInputManifest preserves ordered slots, exact source bytes, target identity, and a declared same-dispatch terminal producer, but does not prove that the producer binding authored or committed the referenced output bytes.
evidence_for: implementations/server/runtime/service.py:5282-5303 requires exact manifest/target identity and ordered slots.
implementations/server/runtime/service.py:5357-5391 verifies source digest and size and requires a binding-output producer in the same dispatch with terminal state.
implementations/server/runtime/service.py:5550-5570 and 5655-5710 persist the manifest and source bytes as artifacts bound to the accepted turn.
implementations/tests/runtime/test_host_workflow_binding.py:366-420 proves rejection before producer termination, acceptance of exact bytes, and rejection after hash drift; the focused suite passed.
evidence_against: The producer terminal event contains state and agent identity, not an output artifact id/hash; a downstream manifest can associate any matching current file with a terminal binding.
missing_evidence: A producer-owned terminal output commitment atomically binding the resolved turn to exact output artifact bytes.
claims.implication_for_harness: The harness can reconstruct what a consumer was given and which producer was declared, but cannot yet defend the stronger claim that the producer committed that result.

claims.statement: Host turn binding preserves the declared recipient coordinates and continuation target: spawn text must equal the confirmed seat prompt, and a follow-up requires a frozen template, a terminal prior turn, and the same bound agent.
evidence_for: implementations/server/runtime/service.py:5482-5535 enforces exact spawn prompt, frozen follow-up template, prior terminal turn, and same agent target.
implementations/server/runtime/service.py:5571-5609 returns an exact prior receipt and rejects a divergent binding retry.
implementations/tests/runtime/test_host_workflow_binding.py:268-285 and 331-364 cover divergent retry and wrong-agent follow-up; the focused suite passed.
evidence_against: The current pair prompt did not start with the required ACI-WORKFLOW-BINDING-V1 marker and no host binding receipt exists for this investigation.
missing_evidence: A host-observed binding receipt for this exact dispatch and a version-pinned adopted-host smoke.
claims.implication_for_harness: The mechanism can prevent recipient drift when invoked, but this dispatch demonstrates that available enforcement is not the same as adopted enforcement.

claims.statement: AgentReferenceDelivery binds a lifecycle-delivered Scout bundle, exact digest and recommendation membership, derived target attempt/seat/agent, insertion ordinal, and effective-input hash in one atomic accepted group.
evidence_for: implementations/server/runtime/service.py:3457-3558 verifies capability scope, same-dispatch source lifecycle, commit-before-delivery order, bundle bytes, and membership.
implementations/server/runtime/service.py:3560-3618 derives the recipient and binds bundle, ordinal, effective-input artifact and hash.
implementations/server/runtime/service.py:3679-3803 and migrations/010_agent_reference_delivery.sql:1-68 commit attempt, input, request, pending effect, and delivery atomically.
implementations/server/runtime/reference_delivery.py:113-157 rejects omitted, duplicated, reordered-at-ordinal, or divergent reference entries.
Five delivery tests and four evidence-reader tests passed in the isolated test root.
evidence_against: Capability scope proves admitted runtime authority, not external authentication of the principal who caused issuance.
missing_evidence: An adopted-host delivery receipt and externally grounded issuer/principal authority.
claims.implication_for_harness: The system can reconstruct exactly which research bundle was admitted into which attempt without inferring that the agent read or used it.

claims.statement: BUS preserves exact official message bytes, message-level producer seat, reveal order, derived recipient, deterministic effective input, atomic acceptance, and stable retry, but its two-seat quorum authority is unsound because closure counts messages rather than distinct eligible seats.
evidence_for: implementations/server/runtime/service.py:2739-2825 orders official messages and freezes their identities and hashes; 2848-2897 requires reveal equality with the frozen collection.
implementations/server/runtime/service.py:2970-3081 derives plan/recipient authority from the binding and scoped capability.
implementations/server/runtime/reveal_delivery.py:52-90 and 140-195 exclude self, retain author/message/hash, preserve reveal order, and bind a deterministic wrapper/effective input.
implementations/server/runtime/migrations/011_bus_reveal_delivery.sql:1-84 stores closure, reveal, plan, materialization, delivery, and receipt identities.
Seven BUS tests passed, covering forged recipient, reverse order, failpoints, stable retry, and semantic drift.
evidence_against: implementations/server/runtime/service.py:2753-2775 sets received_seat_count to len(message rows) and quorum when that count equals two.
implementations/server/runtime/service.py:2060-2067 admits arbitrary nonempty message types outside the Reference Scout prefix condition.
Reviewer executable counterexample published verified position and vote messages from seat-a; closure returned {'received_seat_count': 2, 'quorum_status': 'quorum', 'message_count': 2}.
missing_evidence: Distinct eligible-seat enforcement and per-profile message cardinality/type validation.
claims.implication_for_harness: Message content and attribution remain reconstructible, but the harness must not treat current BUS quorum as evidence of independent collective judgment.

claims.statement: Both specialized delivery paths stop at a sealed launch request with a pending effect; they prove inclusion in effective input, not provider delivery, agent access, cognitive use, or support for a later claim.
evidence_for: implementations/server/runtime/migrations/010_agent_reference_delivery.sql:39-45 permits sandbox_launch_effects only in state pending.
implementations/server/runtime/reference_delivery.py:190-195 records included_in_effective_input=true while access_observed, declared_used, and claim_support are false.
implementations/tests/runtime/test_bus_reveal_delivery.py:625-663 proves materialization starts no subprocess/provider/tool surface and leaves the effect pending.
implementations/tests/runtime/test_agent_reference_evidence_reader.py:46-52 asserts the same evidence boundary.
missing_evidence: A fenced and reconcilable provider-delivery lifecycle.
Separate agent declarations of use and claim-support links.
claims.implication_for_harness: The harness must say 'prepared for delivery' rather than 'consumed' and preserve transport, declared use, and evidentiary support as separate axes.

claims.statement: No generic producer-owned committed-result publication and recipient-acceptance handoff lifecycle is implemented; WorkflowInputManifest is an input-binding mechanism, while Reference Scout and BUS are narrower specialized transports.
evidence_for: Read-only searches across implementations/server/runtime found no handoff.published, handoff.delivered, CommitHandoff, connection_id, or work_result lifecycle.

The available generic workflow path validates current source files and a producer binding at implementations/server/runtime/service.py:5280-5402, but has no producer-owned result commit or recipient acceptance event.
evidence_against: AgentReferenceDelivery and BUS provide specialized bounded delivery contracts, so absence must not be read as absence of all handoff mechanisms.
missing_evidence: A repository-wide generic handoff contract and executable producer-to-recipient acceptance tests.
claims.implication_for_harness: Ordinary agent results cannot yet inherit the same defensible attribution and transfer guarantees as the specialized paths.

gaps.statement: BUS declares two-seat quorum from two message rows, even when both messages come from one seat.
gaps.smallest_next_action: At collection close, validate the declared eligible-seat set, enforce exactly one profile-admitted contribution per seat (or an explicit per-seat cardinality rule), and reject missing, duplicate, and extra seats or message types.
gaps.what_it_buys: One participant can no longer manufacture the appearance of independent agreement.
gaps.completion_evidence: Executable tests for zero, one, duplicate-seat, extra-seat, wrong-type, and valid distinct-seat collections produce the declared reason-coded outcomes.

gaps.statement: A terminal producer binding is not atomically tied to the exact output artifact later consumed.
gaps.smallest_next_action: Commit host-observed resolved output artifact ids/hashes atomically with the producer turn's terminal event and require downstream manifests to reference that commitment.
gaps.what_it_buys: The harness can prove who committed which bytes, not merely who was terminal when a file was labeled as their output.
gaps.completion_evidence: A downstream bind succeeds only for the exact terminally committed artifact and rejects substitution, late mutation, wrong producer, and wrong dispatch.

gaps.statement: There is no generic committed-result publication, delivery, and recipient-acceptance lifecycle for ordinary agent outputs.
gaps.property_lost: Uniform trustworthy transfer across agent work.
gaps.smallest_next_action: Introduce a minimal generic handoff contract joining producer output commitment, intended recipient, ordered context, authority fence, delivery receipt, and acceptance state.
gaps.what_it_buys: All agent-to-agent work can use one reconstructible chain instead of relying on specialized transports or file association.
gaps.completion_evidence: End-to-end tests reconstruct exact producer, recipient, bytes, order, authority, retry, and acceptance for a normal worker-to-reviewer result.

gaps.statement: Launch effects remain pending and no governed provider-delivery reconciliation exists.
gaps.property_lost: Proof that sealed input was actually delivered to the intended execution boundary.
gaps.smallest_next_action: Add fenced claim/start/acknowledge/fail states for the provider effect, binding each receipt to provider invocation, effective-input hash, host agent identity, and retry identity.
gaps.what_it_buys: The harness can prove transport completion or a reason-coded failure without claiming cognitive use.
gaps.completion_evidence: Crash/retry tests converge to one provider delivery receipt or one explicit failed state, with no duplicate execution.

gaps.statement: Transport, declared use, and claim support are not yet recorded as separate downstream relationships.
gaps.property_lost: Honest reconstruction of why a conclusion was reached.
gaps.smallest_next_action: Keep delivery evidence immutable, then add explicit agent declarations of accessed/used entries and claim-to-source support links without auto-promoting transport into use.
gaps.what_it_buys: Reviewers can distinguish available context from used reasoning and from evidence that actually supports a claim.
gaps.completion_evidence: A reconstructed output shows three independently queryable axes—delivered, declared used, and supports claim—with negative and unknown states preserved.

gaps.statement: This dispatch's seats were launched without the mandatory first-line ACI binding marker and have no host binding receipts.
gaps.property_lost: Operational proof that the investigation itself was governed as seats of the parent dispatch.
gaps.smallest_next_action: Record the missed-hook gap in the close record, fix the launch wrapper path, then run one version-pinned adopted-host smoke that emits open, binding, terminal, and close receipts.
gaps.what_it_buys: Evidence that one named host/version actually enforces the workflow binding contract.
gaps.completion_evidence: The smoke produces journal-verifiable receipts for every seat and no orphaned launch; the claim remains version-scoped rather than universal.

gaps.statement: The executable YAML appender used by the isolated fixtures is absent from the current source manifest.
gaps.property_lost: Reproducibility from a fully sealed executable corpus.
gaps.smallest_next_action: Include the appender and its required executable dependencies in the next source manifest.
gaps.what_it_buys: Future handoff proofs can be tied to every executable byte involved in fixture dispatch creation.
gaps.completion_evidence: Manifest validation covers the appender and all focused suites pass from that sealed corpus.

Any generic handoff specification using CommitHandoff/handoff publication-delivery terminology is intended state, not current runtime implementation.
